method_notes: Same fp64 problem on every device; GPU = GB10 cuda:0 (Warp 1.18.0, CUDA 13.0 driver); CPU = the same Warp kernels on the Warp CPU backend (one thread per launch), and a conventional NumPy (vectorised) or SciPy (sparse direct) code.
Grace CPU = GB10's own 20-core Arm (10 Cortex-X925 + 10 Cortex-A725); box CPU = 8-vCPU Intel Xeon VM (Warp 1.19.0). NumPy/SciPy use their default threading.
Warm timings: 1 warm-up excluded, median of 5 (GPU) / 3-5 (CPU; 1 at the largest CPU fin grid), wp.synchronize inside the boundary. Cold: fresh empty kernel cache, first solve includes compile.
Fin solver: Newton + Jacobi-PCG with a host-side dot product per CG iteration, so small grids are latency-bound on the GPU; the production table (585 x 2,560 cells) is run serially.
Thermal MC: one GPU thread per draw (70-step bisection + mass roll-up); host->device copies excluded from the kernel time and reported separately.
Parity = GPU vs CPU agreement (numerical), validation = convergence to an independent 1-D BVP reference + energy balance (physical).
